name: Miacademy
line: Miacademy teaches math in video lessons at a grade the parent picks. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous.
description: AMP vs Miacademy: an all-subject homeschool curriculum with math video lessons at a grade the parent picks, and math where assessment is continuous.
verdict: Miacademy is an online homeschool curriculum for every subject. In math, a learner watches video lessons and then practices, at a grade level the parent chooses [1][4][5]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level and sets the next problem. It keeps a separate level for each part of math, so a learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels. In Miacademy the parent chooses a grade level, and a learner can skip topics already known or switch levels [4][5][6]. We found no placement test on its math pages [4][5][6].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Miacademy the unit is the video lesson: a lesson video with demonstrations, then practice questions, extension activities and review games [4][5]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [11].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In Miacademy the parent can customize the course down to each unit and lesson, and a learner can skip known topics or switch levels [4][5][6]. On MiaPrep, the parent sets the passing grade [3].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Miacademy's kindergarten math follows a spiral that revisits skills [6]. We found no schedule for when a skill returns in the math pages we read [4][5][6]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [10].

reasons.title: What the adult does
reasons.body: In AMP the adult does not plan, teach or grade. Parents and teachers see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind every number, and each lesson has a guide for the adult. In Miacademy the parent chooses the grade level, can customize units and lessons, and keeps a built-in gradebook with grade and attendance reports [1][4][5].

rows.range: Math from counting to algebra and geometry, kindergarten through grade 8 [2]. MiaPrep covers grades 7 to 12 [1].
rows.start: The parent chooses a grade level. We found no placement test on its math pages [4][5][6].
rows.teaching: Video lessons with demonstrations, then practice questions, extension activities and review games [4][5].
rows.next: The course's units and lessons, which the parent can customize. A learner can skip known topics or switch grades [4][5][6].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [4][5][6]. On MiaPrep, the parent sets the passing grade [3].
rows.review: A spiral that revisits skills, in its kindergarten math [6]. No review schedule found.
rows.print: Printable PDF extension activities, and full-course workbooks for some courses in its store [6].
rows.adult: Chooses the grade level, can customize units and lessons, and keeps the gradebook [1][4][5].
rows.reports: A built-in gradebook with downloadable grade and attendance reports [1].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [7][8][9].

theirs: Miacademy is an online homeschool program from Miaplaza Inc. It calls itself "a full K–8 homeschool curriculum" and covers math, reading, science, social studies, electives and world languages [1]. Its sister program, MiaPrep, covers grades 7 to 12 [1].

In math, a learner works at a grade level the parent chooses. Lessons are videos with demonstrations, followed by practice questions, extension activities and review games [4][5]. The parent can customize the course down to each unit and lesson, and a learner can skip known topics or switch levels [5][6]. MiaPrep says its learning path is adjusted daily based on student progress, without saying how [3].
credit: Every subject from kindergarten to grade 8 in one curriculum, math among them [1].
Its early math returns to skills in a spiral [6].

theirs: We found no study of how much students learn with Miacademy. Its accreditation page lists awards and testimonials and makes no claim of studies, test scores or measured outcomes, and its home page and curriculum page link to no research page [1][2][7]. ACS-WASC accredits it as a supplementary education program [7]. Miacademy has no entry in Evidence for ESSA, and the What Works Clearinghouse has no intervention report on it [8][9].
ours: The two findings that bear most on this comparison: practice that mixes and spaces topics scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, in a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [10], and worked examples improve math performance across 55 studies [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want one curriculum for every subject, with math taught in video lessons at a grade you choose.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math, or past grade 8.
You use Miacademy for other subjects and want a separate math program beside it.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Miacademy?
questions.answer: Miacademy teaches math in video lessons at a grade level the parent chooses [4][5]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Miacademy work?
questions.answer: We found no study of how much students learn with Miacademy, on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [7][8][9].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs, and a learner can use Miacademy for other subjects and AMP for math. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
